# arcgis-download-features-button

**DEPRECATED**. Use `arcgis-hub-download-list-item` instead. This component will be removed once the new component is fully tested and ready for production.

The `arcgis-download-features-button` encapsulates all the logic needed to make a `createReplica` call to an ArcGIS Feature Server.

When clicked, the button will fetch a download url from the feature server and emit the url as part of an `ArcgisDownloadSuccess` event. It will not trigger the native download ui. The consuming client is responsible for triggering the actual download with the provided download url.

`item` (or `server`) and `layers` are required arguments. All others are used to fine-tune the resulting downloadable file.

It should be noted that when passing in `filter-geometry`, it's spatial reference MUST have an accurate `wkid` property attached. `latestWkid` will not be recognized.

## Item vs. Server
To give consuming developers more flexibility, the `arcgis-download-button` has 2 props that 
can be used to determine the targeted feature service's url:
- `item`: The portal item representing the targeted feature service (or one of it's layers). When 
passed in, the component will parse the targeted feature service's root url from the item's url. 
Additional item information will also be used when emitting telemetry.
- `server`: Either the root url to the targeted feature service OR its service definition object
with `url` as a property. `server` takes precedence over `item`.

Only one of these properties is required for the button to work. However when both are passed in, `item` will
be used exclusively for telemetry and `server` will be used to determine the feature service's url.

## Events
The `arcgis-download-features-button` will emit one of two events after being clicked:
- `arcGisDownloadSuccess`
- `arcGisDownloadError`

`arcGisDownloadSuccess` contains the following details:
```js
{
  serviceUrl, // the provided service url, used to correlate requests
  fileFormat, // the provided file format, used to correlate requests
  downloadUrl // the final url that points to the downloadable replica
}
```

`arcGisDownloadError` contains the following details:
```js
{
  serviceUrl, // the provided service url, used to correlate requests
  fileFormat, // the provided file format, used to correlate requests
  error // the raw ArcGISRequestError received
}
```

## Example - Fetch all data from the specified layers
```hbs
<arcgis-download-features-button
  server="https://services2.arcgis.com/zNjnZafDYCAJAbN0/arcgis/rest/services/Street_ROW_Trees/FeatureServer"
  layers="2">
  Download
</arcgis-download-features-button>
```

## Example - Fetch all data from the specified layers as a CSV
```hbs
<arcgis-download-features-button
  server="https://services2.arcgis.com/zNjnZafDYCAJAbN0/arcgis/rest/services/Street_ROW_Trees/FeatureServer"
  layers="2"
  file-format="csv">
  Download
</arcgis-download-features-button>
```

## Example - Fetch data from the specified layers that match a given query

```hbs
<arcgis-download-features-button
  server="https://services2.arcgis.com/zNjnZafDYCAJAbN0/arcgis/rest/services/Street_ROW_Trees/FeatureServer"
  layers=[
    {
      id: 2,
      where: "field IN ('value')"
    }
  ]>
  Download
</arcgis-download-features-button>
```

## Example - Fetch data from the specified layers within a geographic boundary

```hbs
<arcgis-download-features-button
  server="https://services2.arcgis.com/zNjnZafDYCAJAbN0/arcgis/rest/services/Street_ROW_Trees/FeatureServer"
  layers="2"
  filter-geometry={
    type: “extent”,
    spatialReference: { wkid: 4326 },
    xmin: -118.16,
    ymin: 34.14,
    xmax: -118.12,
    ymax: 34.16
  }>
  Download
</arcgis-download-features-button>
```

## Example - Use a Service Definition Object
```hbs
<arcgis-download-features-button
  server={
    capabilities: 'Extract',
    supportedExportFormats: 'csv',
    url: 'https://services2.arcgis.com/zNjnZafDYCAJAbN0/arcgis/rest/services/Street_ROW_Trees/FeatureServer'
  }
  layers="2">
  Download
</arcgis-download-features-button>
```

## Example - Use an Item
```hbs
<arcgis-download-features-button
  item={
    id: '9001',
    access: 'public',
    type: 'Feature Service',
    url: 'https://services2.arcgis.com/zNjnZafDYCAJAbN0/arcgis/rest/services/Street_ROW_Trees/FeatureServer/2'
  }
  layers="2">
  Download
</arcgis-download-features-button>
```

## Example - Use Both Item and Server
```hbs
<arcgis-download-features-button
  item={
    id: '9001',
    access: 'public',
    type: 'Feature Service',
    url: 'https://services2.arcgis.com/zNjnZafDYCAJAbN0/arcgis/rest/services/Street_ROW_Trees/FeatureServer/2'
  }
  server={
    capabilities: 'Extract',
    supportedExportFormats: 'csv',
    url: 'https://services2.arcgis.com/zNjnZafDYCAJAbN0/arcgis/rest/services/Street_ROW_Trees/FeatureServer'
  }
  layers="2">
  Download
</arcgis-download-features-button>
```

## References
- The [createReplica documentation](https://developers.arcgis.com/rest/services-reference/enterprise/create-replica.htm) is incomplete and sometimes incorrect, but provides a good overview for those needing more specialized downloads
- The `IGeometry` interface we use is based off [Esri's Geometry Class](https://developers.arcgis.com/rest/services-reference/enterprise/create-replica.htm). However, our implementation requires the `type` and `spatialReference` fields in order to infer some parameters for `createReplica`.

# arcgis-download-list

**DEPRECATED**. Use `arcgis-hub-download-list` instead. This component will be removed once the new component is fully tested and ready for production.

The `arcgis-download-list` is a dynamic wrapper of the `arcgis-download-features-button`. When given a Feature Service, the component determines which download formats the service supports and renders a button for each format. Whenever a button is clicked and a file is ready for download, the list will trigger the browser's native download ui.

Just like the underlying `arcgis-download-features-button`, the `arcgis-download-list` requires both `item` (or `server`) and `layers` in order to work. All parameters will be passed through to each download button. See the documentation for `arcgis-download-features-button` for more details on the structure of these parameters.

## Item vs. Server
To give flexibility to consuming developers, the `arcgis-download-list` can use 2 props to determine supported formats for a given feature service:
- `item`: The portal item representing the targeted feature service (or one of it's layers). When 
passed in, the component will parse the targeted feature service's root url from the item's url.
Once the service's url has been parsed, the component will reach out to the service and get its
most up to date definition. Additionally, item information will be used to enrich telemetry.
- `server`: Either the root url to the targeted feature service OR its service definition object
with `url` as a property. `server` takes precedence over `item`. When `server` is a url, the 
component will reach out to the service and get its most up to date definition. When `server` is
a service definition object, no fetching will occur.

Only one of these properties is required for the list to work. However when both are passed in, `item` will be used exclusively for telemetry and `server` will be used to determine the feature service's definition.

**Example: Use Item**

```
<arcgis-download-list 
  item={
    id: '9001',
    access: 'public',
    type: 'Feature Service',
    url: 'https://services2.arcgis.com/zNjnZafDYCAJAbN0/arcgis/rest/services/Street_ROW_Trees/FeatureServer/2'
  }
  layers="2"
>
```

**Example: Use Server (URL)**

```
<arcgis-download-list 
  server="https://services2.arcgis.com/zNjnZafDYCAJAbN0/arcgis/rest/services/Street_ROW_Trees/FeatureServer" 
  layers="2"
>
```

**Example: Use Server (Definition Object)**

```
<arcgis-download-list 
  server={
    supportedExportFormats: "csv",
    capabilities: "Extract",
    service-url="https://services2.arcgis.com/zNjnZafDYCAJAbN0/arcgis/rest/services/Street_ROW_Trees/FeatureServer" 
  }
  layers="2"
>
```

Finally, the list has three ui layouts: a card view, a link view, and a dropdown view. The list defaults to card view.

**Example: Card View**

```
<arcgis-download-list 
  server="https://services2.arcgis.com/zNjnZafDYCAJAbN0/arcgis/rest/services/Street_ROW_Trees/FeatureServer" 
  layers="2"
/>
```

OR

```
<arcgis-download-list 
  server="https://services2.arcgis.com/zNjnZafDYCAJAbN0/arcgis/rest/services/Street_ROW_Trees/FeatureServer" 
  layers="2" 
  layout="cards"
/>
```

**Example: List View**

```
<arcgis-download-list 
  server="https://services2.arcgis.com/zNjnZafDYCAJAbN0/arcgis/rest/services/Street_ROW_Trees/FeatureServer" 
  layers="2" 
  layout="links"
/>
```

**Example: Dropdown View**

```
<arcgis-download-list 
  server="https://services2.arcgis.com/zNjnZafDYCAJAbN0/arcgis/rest/services/Street_ROW_Trees/FeatureServer" 
  layers="2" 
  layout="dropdown"
/>
```

Renders dropdown with options to add content to a Hub entity

## Use cases

### Query-based configuration

We support both adding existing entities and creating new entities to add to the specified query. This is how the component is configured when exposed on arcgis-hub-gallery.

```jsx
const query = {
  targetEntity: "item",
  filters: [
    {
      predicates: [
        {
          group: "4f795ef243da4649a0ebd436e071c88b",
          type: "Hub Initiative"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
};
<arcgis-hub-add-content query={query} />
```

### Workflow-based configuration

This configuration can be used to create specific entities but targetEntities cannot be mixed.

```jsx
const config = {
  create: {
    workflow: "create",
    targetEntity: "group",
    types: [
      "Group"
    ]
  }
};
<arcgis-hub-add-content config={config} />
```

### Workspace global header

We support creating new entities (not selecting existing) and adding them to any group the user has permission to share content to.

```jsx
<arcgis-hub-add-content allow-group-selection />
```

### Site header

We support creating new entities (not selecting existing) and adding them to any group in the site's catalogs.

```jsx
  <arcgis-hub-add-content catalog={catalog} />
```

## Near term enhancements:
- more/better docs
- more/better tests on the components and the machines
- we will need to have an entity-putter-inner component (where today we just use a gallery of groups in the second step) at some point

## Known issues:
- the use case where we explicitly pass in groupIds is not implemented
  - really we need to get clear on what that means - i think it is:
    - we only use groupIds if the user also passes allowGroupSelection=false and we simply share to the specified groupIds without showing the group selection step
- from randy: if there is a groupid that the user is not able to share the event with, the whole operation will fail, but we may be able to circumvent that in shareentitytogroups by stripping out the groups that the user cannot share to; but as a side effect of that, it would break the receipt

- tighten up the typing
- DRY up the machine

# arcgis-hub-calendar

Arcgis-hub-calendar is a wrapper component for the Full Calendar library for use with arcgis-hub-gallery. The calendar emits events when dates and date ranges are selected so that the gallery can filter search results. The selectable date range can be configured, and the maximum number of events displayed on a calendar date can be adjusted to accomodate for the available space the calendar is displayed in.

Example 1: Basic usage

```
<arcgis-hub-calendar 
  searchResults={[IHubSearchResult]}
/>
```

Example 2: Calendar with restricted selectable date range

```
<arcgis-hub-calendar 
  searchResults={[IHubSearchResult]}
  maxSelectableDate={number | string | Date}
  minSelectableDate={number | string | Date}
/>
```

Example 3: Calendar with limited events per day displayed

```
<arcgis-hub-calendar 
  searchResults={[IHubSearchResult]}
  maxEventsPerDay={number}
/>
```

# arcgis-hub-catalog-builder

The `arcgis-hub-catalog-builder` is a composite field for configuring an `IHubCatalog`.

It can be used both independently or as a field in a schema-driven editing experience

## How to extend

As we continue to build out additional services for Hub-backed entities, we can extend the catalog builder to surface these target entities in the UI for configuration:

1. Update the default array of `targetEntities` to surface in the UI to include your new `targetEntity`
2. Add a translation string for the new `targetEntity` to the locale file

These two steps alone are enough to start surfacing the new `targetEntity` as an option for configuration in the UI. For more information on how to adjust/extend the filter options that are available for the `targetEntity`, visit the `arcgis-hub-predicates-builder` docs.

# arcgis-hub-discussions

A component that encapsulates the logic and UI related to contributing to free-form
discussions about an IHubContent or IGroup. The component can fetch it's dependencies
from minimal subsets of mostly primitive properties else directy receive properties
as a micro-optimization to prevent unnecessary refetching of dependencies when they're
already available in a higher scope.

Example 1: Discussions on a piece of content

```html
<arcgis-hub-discussions
  discussion="hub://content/31c"
/>
```

Example 2: Render a specific thread for a given parentId

```html
<arcgis-hub-discussions
  discussion="hub://content/31c"
  parentId="4f9"
/>
```

Example 3: Render a specific parent and reply

```html
<arcgis-hub-discussions
  discussion="hub://content/31c"
  parentId="4f9"
  postId="2n5"
/>
```

# arcgis-hub-discussions-post-editor

A component that encapsulates the logic and UI related to authoring posts and replies via
the Hub Discussions API. The component can fetch it's dependencies from minimal subsets of
mostly primitive properties else directly receive properties as a micro-optimization to
prevent unnecessary refetching of dependencies when they're already available in a higher
scope.

Example 1: Create a new parent post given `context` and `discussion`. Will default to the channel selection view.

```html
<arcgis-hub-discussions-post-editor
  discussion="hub://content/e3b"
/>
```

Example 2: Create a new parent post given `context`, `discussion` & `channelId`. Pre-selects the channel and skips directly to the post content authoring view.

```html
<arcgis-hub-discussions-post-editor
  discussion="hub://content/e3b"
  channelId="b4c"
/>
```

Example 3: Create a new parent post given `context`, `discussion`, `channelGroupIds` & `channelAccess`. Skips directly to the post content authoring view. Will
re-use a channel if one exists with the given `channelGroupIds` and `channelAccess` values, else it will create a new channel at the time the first parent post
is created.

```html
<arcgis-hub-discussions-post-editor
  discussion="hub://content/e3b"
  channelGroupIds={['4c2']}
  channelAccess="private"
/>
```

Example 4: Edit a parent post or reply given `context` & `postId`.

```html
<arcgis-hub-discussions-post-editor
  postId="b4c"
/>
```

Example 5: Create a reply to a parent post given `context` & `parentId`.

```html
<arcgis-hub-discussions-post-editor
  parentId="b4c"
/>
```

# arcgis-hub-discussions-thread

A component that encapsulates the logic and UI related to render a "thread". The component can fetch it's
dependencies from minimal subsets of mostly primitive properties else directy receive properties as a
micro-optimization to prevent unnecessary refetching of dependencies when they're already available in
a higher scope. A "thread" is the composition of either:
 
1. A parent post, collection of all replies, and a post editor to create new replies
2. A parent post and a single reply
 
Example 1: Render a parent post and all replies

```html
<arcgis-hub-discussions-thread
  channelId="g3f"
  parentId="31c"
/>
```
 
Example 2: Render a parent post and a single reply

```html
<arcgis-hub-discussions-thread
  channelId="g3f"
  parentId="31c"
  postId="4fc"
/>
```

# arcgis-hub-download-list-item

The <arcgis-hub-download-list-item> is responsible for handling user interaction, initiating download requests, and reporting progress to the end user. However, there must be an <arcgis-hub-download-manager> component at the root of the application or download requests **will not be handled**.

Essentially, <arcgis-hub-download-list-item> emits an event to the DOM body with all the necessary data to initiate a download request. It also attaches a unique jobId to the event detail for tracking purposes. <arcgis-hub-download-manager> receives the request and initiates the actual download process. It reports progress back to the <arcgis-hub-download-report> via update events that can be listened to on the DOM body. <arcgis-hub-download-list-item> then updates the UI according to the payloads that it receives.

NOTE: <arcgis-hub-download-list-item> is purely a presentational component and will not invoke the actual download to the browser. See <arcgis-hub-download-manager> for more.

    - **Web map** - the URL we get from the map viewer on AGO renders the editor instead of the viewer when the user is authed. However, at the bottom of the page, there is a URL for sharing, that one renders the viewer. The difference between the two URLs is that `/mapviewer` renders the editor and `/webappviewer` the viewer. 
    - **Web scene** - AGO provides 2 URLs - a regular one and a short one. If we use the regular one for both private and public scenes, when the user is authed, it will load the scene editor. If anonymous, the public one will be loaded as the scene viewer and the private one will not be loaded with either URI. If we use the short one, the public one will load the viewer, the private one will not be loaded even when authed.

Component that renders Entity breadcrumbs.

The breadcrumbs can be passed into the component as a `path`, which the component them parses and fetches all the entities and constructs the links.

```html
<arcgis-hub-entity-breadcrumbs 
  path="/sites/f0094b90e77d426f918437561a80677b/projects/aa9e680b6b524611be96842ea4ff48">
  </arcgis-hub-entity-breadcrumbs>
```

Alternatively, the host application can pass in `IHubEntityBreadcrumb` objects. The advantage of this option is that if the host has already fetched entities for segments of the breadcrumbs, those can be passed in and avoid fetching the information.

For example, in the Hub run-time application there is always a "site" defined, and this is usually the first segment of the breadcrumbs path (labeled at "Home"), thus the host application can pass that in, instead of having the component fetch the site object in order to get the url.

The component delegates to the `Breadcrumbs` functional component for rendering of the menu item entries.

This is the hero slot

About

This is slotted about

 ``` **Slots** are a stop-gap. We expect all existing entity view's to be migrated so that the slots are not used. ## Sub-Components Internally, `arcgis-hub-entity-view` it will determine what hero & about components to render, along with tabs for additional configured content/embeds etc. The following sections detail how to configure each. ## Configuring Hero Sub-Component The `arcgis-hub-entity-view` will render the `arcgis-hub-entity-hero` component, unless the entity type is present in the `HeroViews` array defined in `config.ts` ```js export const HeroViews: ITypeSpecificViewDefinition[] = [ { entity: 'event', component: 'arcgis-hub-event-hero', } ] ``` Custom Hero components should follow the patterns and props in `arcgis-hub-entity-hero` ## Configuring About Sub-Component The `arcgis-hub-entity-view` delegates to `arcgis-hub-entity-catalogs` component to render the tabs which will include the About view for the entity, as well as the catalogs and type-specific views. By default, `arcgis-hub-entity-catalogs` will render the `arcgis-hub-entity-about` component, unless there is an entry in the `AboutViews` array defined in `config.ts` ``` export const AboutViews: ITypeSpecificViewDefinition[] = [ { entity: 'event', component: 'arcgis-hub-event-about', }, { entity: 'project', component: 'arcgis-hub-project-about', } ] ``` Custom About components should follow the patterns and props in `arcgis-hub-entity-about` ## Type Specific Views Some entities have highly specific views that are only relevant to them. We define these in the `TypeSpecificViews` in the `config.ts` file ``` export const TypeSpecificViews: ITypeSpecificViewDefinition[] = [ { // What entity does thie apply to? entity: 'project', // OPTIONAL permission - typically used for gating permission: 'hub:project:view:metrics', // i18n string i18nLabel: 'tabs.metrics', // Component that will be rendered component: 'arcgis-hub-project-metrics-view', } ] ``` Type-specific Views will be passed the entity via prop, and context should be pulled from the store. For more information, please see the [UI Architecture of ArcGIS Hub](https://confluencewikidev.esri.com/display/Hub/UI+Architecture%3A+Views%2C+Workspaces+and+Layouts)

# arcgis-hub-groups-card

The `arcgis-hub-groups-card` component is for embedding a select list of teams which are sorted by the order in the groups array.

## Example

```hbs
<arcgis-hub-groups-card title="Featured Teams" groups={["123abc", "sgba453", "456def"]}>
</arcgis-hub-groups-card>
```

## ArcGIS Enterprise

By default, the queries will be run against ArcGIS Online. ArcGIS Enterprise can be utilized by setting the `portal` property

## ArcGIS Enterprise Example

```hbs
<arcgis-hub-groups-card title="Featured Teams" groups={["123abc", "sgba453", "456def"]} portal="https://myserver.org/gis">
</arcgis-hub-groups-card>
```

### Authentication

To make authenticated requests, the `.context` property must be set on the element itself. See the [ArcGISContextManager documentation](https://esri.github.io/hub.js/api/common/ArcGISContextManager/) for additional details.

# arcgis-hub-predicates-builder

The `arcgis-hub-predicates-builder` is a composite field for configuring an array of `IPredicates`.

It can be used both independently or as a field in a schema-driven editing experience.

## How to extend
The `arcgis-hub-predicates-builder` is an extremely flexible and extensible system that's primarily powered by several schema-based config hashes. Based on these configurations, we dynamically generate + populate the fields that make up the predicate's editing experience.

### Extending an existing predicate property to be available for a new target entity:

If an `IPredicateConfig` already exists for a particular property (see the `getPredicateConfig.ts` util), and you simply want this option to be available for a specific target entity:

1. Ensure your `targetEntity` has a corresponding `<Entity>PredicateProperty` type defined in `types.ts`. This indicates which predicate properties are valid for the given `targetEntity`.
2. Add the existing predicate property to the `targetEntity's` `<Entity>PredicateProperty`.
3. Add your `targetEntity` to the relevant `IPropertyConfig.targetEntities` array which specifies which target entities the property can be applied to.

### Extending the predicate builder to support a new property:

If an `IPredicateConfig` does NOT already exist for a particular property of interest (see the `getPredicateConfig.ts` util):

1. Add the new predicate property to the relevant `targetEntity's` `<Entity>PredicateProperty`. Note: this property should correspond to a property that we can serialize/transform into a query/parameter to send to relevant API(s).
2. Create an `IPropertyConfig` for the new property in `getPropertyConfig.ts`
3. Create an `IPredicateConfig` for the new property in `getPredicateConfig.ts`

# arcgis-hub-tree-facet

Unlike `arcgis-facet-options` which displays all options at a flat level, `arcgis-hub-tree-facet` displays the hierarchy of related options for a more logical user experience.

However, instead of requiring consumers to construct a complex tree object, all consumers need is a flat array of options. Each option should have a key that expresses the full path hierarchy of the option. The facet will parse these keys and automatically generate the correct tree structure.

This decision to operate on flat arrays shields other parts of the gallery subsystem from having to do tree manipulation / traversal and is consistent with other gallery patterns at this time.

Example:

```
<arcgis-hub-tree-facet
 facet={
    label: "Categories",
    key: "categories",
    display: "tree",
    options: [
      {
        label: 'child_1 (1)'
        key: "/categories/parent/child_1",
        predicates: [...]
      },
      {
        label: 'parent (2)'
        key: "/categories/parent",
        predicates: [...]
      },
      {
        label: 'child_2 (1)'
        key: "/categories/parent/child_2",
        predicates: [...]
      },
    ]
  }
/>
```

# arcgis-hub-workspace-dirty-state-modal
The dirty state modal is a bit of friction added to the navigation within Workspaces whilst editing. It intentionally obstructs a user's ability to navigate to a new pane, tab, or modal that would cause overlapping, unsaved edits to an entity. 

For example: while editing a content entity's description on the details pane, if a user has not saved their changes, the dirty state modal would appear when trying to transition to another pane or the share modal.

Another example: while editing a site's collections in the content pane's collection tab, if a user has not saved their changes, the dirty state modal would appear when trying to switch to the catalog configuration tab.

An important detail regarding the props of the dirty state modal is whether or not you pass an `href` or `pane` in. If you are navigating to a new `href` or `tab`, the "Discard changes"/confirm button in the dirty state modal would need to be wrapped in a workspace link to notify the workspace a dirty state modal should appear. If you don't pass in either one but a dirty state is present, we assume that a save is required before accessing a modal or continuing in another direction on the same pane and tab.

a tooltip.

# hub-composite-input-expression-set

 ## Overview
The `hub-composite-input-expression-set` renders an expression builder component that creates a list of expressions with which to create a filtering clause (WHERE clause, SQL statement, etc.). The expression-set does so by taking in an array of `IField` objects and allowing the user to create statements from them (e.x. "type" is exactly "value", "id" is between 0 and 4, etc.)

The `hub-composite-input-expression-set` returns an `IExpression[]` that looks like the following:

```ts
[
  {
    key: `string`, // unique key to use internally
    field: `IField`, // IField object
    values: [] // values that are associated with the expression -- currently 0 - 2 values allowed
  }
]
```

These can then be transformed easily into a `where` clause to use for filtering (`buildWhereClause` in `metrics.ts`). We pass the expressions in an `IExpression[]` to be able to render expressions with the configuration editor easily rather than emitting a `where` clause immediately. 

## Field Types
The expression-set will render different input types depending on the field type. 

### string (`esriFieldTypeString`)
The options for strings are:
- `matches exactly`: one free input will render

Note: if the field has domain coded values, then the rendered input will be a `hub-field-input-select` and only allow the coded values to be selected.

### numeric
The options for numeric field types are:
- `between`: two free numeric inputs will render

### date
The options for date field types are:
- `between`: two date picker inputs will render

 ## Usage
 The following `schema` and `uiSchema` show how you might declare this type of field when building out your editor's `schema` and `uiSchema`. They represent the `schema` and `uiSchema` for a single property:

 ### `schema`

 ```ts
 {
  type: "array",
 }
 ```

 ### `uiSchema`

 ```ts
 {
  ..., 
  type: 'Control",
  options: {
    fields, // the fields to build from in the expression set
    control: 'hub-composite-input-expression-set'
  }
 }
 ```


#### `uiSchema.options`
`uiSchema.options` specific to `hub-composite-input-expression-set`

| option | type | required | default | description |
| ------ | ---- | -------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `fields` | `IField[]` | `false` | `[]` | an array of fields to allow to be filterable

# hub-field-input-combobox

The `hub-field-input-combobox` renders a combobox field in the configuration editor.

## Usage

 The following `schema` and `uiSchema` show how you might declare this type of field when building out your editor's `schema` and `uiSchema`. They represent the `schema` and `uiSchema` for a single property:

### `schema`

```ts
{
  type: "array",
  items: {
    type: "string",
    enum: ["option1", "option2", "option3", "option4"],
  },
  maxItems: 3
}
```
### `uiSchema`

```ts
{
  ..., // see all IUiSchemaElement properties in arcgis-configuration-editor docs
  type: 'Control',
  options: {
    ..., // see non-field specific options in arcgis-configuration-editor-field docs
    control: 'hub-field-input-combobox',
    items: [
      { value: "option1", label: "Option 1", icon: 'icon1' },
      { value: "option2", label: "Option 2", icon: 'icon2' },
      { value: "option3", label: "Option 3", icon: 'icon3' },
      { value: "option4", label: "Option 4", icon: 'icon4' }
    ],
    allowCustomValues: true,
    selectionMode: 'multiple'
  }
}
```

#### `uiSchema.options`
`uiSchema.options` specific to `hub-field-input-combo` 

| option | type | required | default | description | 
| ------ | ---- | -------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `items` | `IUiSchemaComboboxItem[]` | `false` | `undefined` | an array of options to pass into the `calcite-combobox` |
| `allowCustomValues` | `boolean` | `false` | `undefined` | when `true`, allows entry of custom values, which are not in the original set of items. If an `enum` is defined in the `schema`, this will be ignored and set to `false` |
| `selectionMode` | `string` | `false` | `multiple` | specifies the selection mode of the combobox (options: `multiple`, `single`, `ancestors`) |


### Adding children
To nest combobox items, you can follow the following syntax in your uiSchema:

```ts
{
  ..., // see all IUiSchemaElement properties in arcgis-configuration-editor docs
  type: 'Control',
  options: {
    ..., // see non-field specific options in arcgis-configuration-editor-field docs
    control: 'hub-field-input-combobox',
    items: [
      { value: "option1", label: "Option 1", icon: 'icon1' },
      { value: "option2", label: "Option 2", icon: 'icon2' },
      { value: "option3", label: "Option 3", icon: 'icon3' },
      { value: "option4", label: "Option 4", icon: 'icon4',
      children: [ // use a children array to designate a child of an item
        {
          value: "option4-child1",
          label: "Option 4 child 1",
        }
      ] }
    ],
    // ...anything else you want
  }
}
```

Child items will be nested in the ui.

If the `selectionMode` provided is `multiple`, selecting a child will _not_ automatically select the parent.

If the `selectionMode` provided is `ancestors`, selection a child _will_ automatically select the parent(s).
components.docs:
The Combobox component renders a list of items in a calcite combobox
as calcite combobox items. Users have the option to allow entries of custom values
with the allowCustomValues option. They may also specify the selection mode of the combobox
with the selectionMode option(single, multiple or ancestors).
The Combobox works for both pre-defined/static and dynamic options.
For pre-defined/static option, an enum is provided in the schema,
all items in uiSchema.options.items will be rendered in the combobox.
For dynamic option, an enum is not provided in the schema,
items in uiSchema.options.items that are not defined in schema.items will be ignored.
NOTE, if an enum is provided in the schema, allowCustomValues will also be ignored.

# hub-field-input-scheduler
The scheduler component is a flexible tool for those making use of the already flexible configuration editor. It takes in an initial value, or defaults to `mode: "automatic"`, and allows developers to provide different scheduling options. These options are know as `cadence`s, and those are `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`, and `yearly` -- each of these being `mode: "scheduled"`. There are two other modes that don't require cadences, `mode: "automatic"` and `mode: "manual"`. 

These options only set the object's schedule, but the component has no additional knowledge of outside APIs or context. It is up to the developer to wrap the schedule and make use of it within hub.js.

Please view the harness examples for more in depth deconstruction.

- [Follow-up Tech Ticket - 10156 - Select and Single formats + validation](https://devtopia.esri.com/dc/hub/issues/10156)

## Initial Contributors
- Design: Sean Kintz
- Backend: Santash Shrestha
- Frontend: Aaron Putterman
- Product: Thomas Hervey

## Why a new component? Why not a composite/nested configuration editor field?
I had a lengthy discussion with Sean and Klara about the design of the scheduler component, and relayed the takeaways to Thomas. It sounded like the best course of action is to create a component wrapped by the configuration editors that does not nest another config-editor inside for accessibility concerns. Due to limitations of the calcite component library, the design team was unsure if removing the dynamic inputs from the radio group list was a sustainable practice for those who use screen readers or keyboard navigations. Ultimately, creating a new reusable component over nesting configuration editor instances would result in less technical debt for us in the long run.
 
As an alternative, for developer, designer, and consumer sake, we included the format prop, which with you team's designer's opinion, will allow you to format your scheduler component with either a calcite-select or calcite-radio-group. This way varying option lengths will provide optimal experiences for users.

## Revisiting in September/October 2024
After a rushed release attempt in late September to support scheduled downloads on the content views, we ultimately decided to hold off on large changes to the scheduler. Instead, we settled on updating the existing scheduler formats. During this time, we were also undergoing staff changes and a release freeze prior to the 2024 presidential election.

We first removed support for the `radio` format, which for a11y + product reasons, did not align with our current or future designs. We then changed the inputs that appear when selecting a scheduled frequency to display in a vertical format, rather than in a row horizontally. This change to vertical styles allows us to provide more helper text, and squeeze the scheduler input into smaller spaces (like a side panel or modal).

These decisions were discussed in two meetings, one on October 3 between Platform, Discovery, and design, and the other conversation on October 4 by Discovery and Design.

## `schema` example
```json
{
  ...
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    schedule: {
      type: 'object',
    },
  }
}
```
## `uiSchema` example
```json
{
    label: 'Scheduler Input',
    scope: '/properties/schedule',
    type: 'Control',
    options: {
        control: 'hub-field-input-scheduler',
        format: 'select',
        inputs: [
            { label: "Default", type: "automatic", },
            { label: "Daily", type: "daily", expandedHelperText: "Each day at" },
            { label: "Weekly", type: "weekly", expandedHelperText: "Each week on" },
            { label: "Monthly", type: "monthly", expandedHelperText: "Each month on" },
            { label: "Yearly", type: "yearly", expandedHelperText: "Each year on" },
            { label: "Manual", type: "manual", helperActionIcon: "information-f", helperActionText: "Use this option to manually update the search index and cached download files for this item." }
        ],
    }
}
```

## Providing different options to the `uiSchema`
The uiSchema is meant to be a flexible casing for a variety of options that the scheduler supports. 

First, developers and designers need to decide what the proper viewing format should be for viewers that provides the best UX.

| Format | Description                                                                                                          |
+--------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| select | Options are contained with a calcite select/dropdown.                                                                |
| single | Only shows the expanded section's content. Provide a single `option` in the inputs array to make use of this format. |

Each input option supports the following properties.

| Property           | Type   | Description                                                                                                           |
+--------------------+--------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| label              | string | The label that appears in the select                                                     |
| type               | string | "daily", "weekly", "monthly", "yearly", "automatic", and "manual"                                                     |
| expandedHelperText | string | If the selected option has an expanded section for further user input, this text will be displayed above those inputs |
| helperActionIcon   | string | A calcite icon that appears next to the option; when hovered over, shows the `helperActionText`                       |
| helperActionText   | string | A string of helper text that appears as a tooltip next to the option                                                  |


## Validation
After discussing validation options with Jordan and Julianne, we settled on adding the validation into the scheduler component itself due to it _not_ being a compositie component.

Validation messages that you might encounter are related to required fields that have empty inputs or the `value` of the scheduler being invalid. Either of these would disable the save button in the configuration editor.

Messages include: 
- "Please select a time."
- "Please select a timezone."
- "Please select a day."
- "Please select a date."
- "Please select a month."

Not an error but worth including here:
- "Time will round to the nearest hour" will show below hour inputs until Calcite makes improvements to the `step` attribute on their components.


## Relevant Interfaces and Types
[https://github.com/Esri/hub.js/blob/master/packages/common/src/core/types/IHubSchedule.ts](https://github.com/Esri/hub.js/blob/master/packages/common/src/core/types/IHubSchedule.ts)

The scheduler component is a flexible tool for those making use of the already flexible configuration editor. It takes in an initial value, or defaults to `mode: "automatic"`, and allows developers to provide different scheduling options. These options are know as `cadence`s, and those are `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`, and `yearly` -- each of these being `mode: "scheduled"`. There are two other modes that don't require cadences, `mode: "automatic"` and `mode: "manual"`. 

These options only set the object's schedule, but the component has no additional knowledge of outside APIs or context. It is up to the developer to wrap the schedule and make use of it within hub.js.

Please view the harness examples for more in depth deconstruction.

# hub-field-input-select

The `hub-field-input-select` renders a dropdown select field

## Usage

 The following `schema` and `uiSchema` show how you might declare this type of field when building out your editor's `schema` and `uiSchema`. They represent the `schema` and `uiSchema` for a single property: 

### `schema`

```ts
{
  type: 'string',
  default: 'option2',
  enum: [ 'option1', 'option2', 'option3' ]
}
```

### `uiSchema`

```ts
{
  ..., // see all IUiSchemaElement properties in arcgis-configuration-editor docs
  type: 'Control',  
  options: {
    ..., // see non-field specific options in arcgis-configuration-editor-field docs
    control: 'hub-field-input-select',
    enum: {
      i18nScope: 'some.scope',
      labels: [ "Label 1", "Label 2" ]
    }
  }
}
```

#### `uiSchema.options` 
`uiSchema.options` specific to `hub-field-input-select` 

| option | type | required | description | 
| ------ | -------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `enum.i18nScope` | `string` | `false` | i18nScope to translate enum values |
| `labels` | `string[]` | `false` | translated labels to apply to schema enum values - ordering is assumed to match enum

# hub-field-input-tile-select

The `hub-field-input-tile-select` renders a tile-select field.

## Usage

The tile-select field can be used as a group of checkboxes or a group of radio buttons by setting the `type` property in `uiSchema.options`. 

### Radio type
Note that the value returned from `hub-field-input-tile-select` when set to `radio` type selection is `string`.
The following `schema` and `uiSchema` show how you might declare the tile-select field as a radio group when building out your editor's `schema` and `uiSchema`. They represent the `schema` and `uiSchema` for a single property: 

#### `schema` when using radio mode
```ts
{
    type: "string",
    enum: ["option1", "option2", "option3"]
}
```

#### `uiSchema` when using radio mode
```ts    
{
    ...,  // see all IUiSchemaElement properties in arcgis-configuration-editor docs
    type: 'Control',
    options: {
         ..., // see non-field specific options in arcgis-configuration-editor-field docs
        control: 'hub-field-input-tile-select'
        labels: ["option1", "option2", "option3"],
        descriptions: ["desc1", "desc2", "desc3"],
        icons: ["icon1", "icon2", "icon3" ],
        type: "radio",
    }
},
```

### Checkbox type
Note that the value returned from `hub-field-input-tile-select` when set to `checkbox` type selection is `string[]`.

The following `schema` and `uiSchema` show how you might declare the tile-select field as a checkbox group when building out your editor's `schema` and `uiSchema`. They represent the `schema` and `uiSchema` for a single property: 

### `schema` when using checkbox mode
```ts
{
    type: "array",
    items: {
        type: "string",
        enum: ["option1", "option2", "option3"],
    }
}
```

### `uiSchema` when using checkbox mode
```ts
{
    ..., // see all IUiSchemaElement properties in arcgis-configuration-editor docs
    type: "Control",
    options: {
        ...,  // see non-field specific options in arcgis-configuration-editor-field docs
        control: 'hub-field-input-tile-select',
        labels: ["option1", "option2", "option3"],
        descriptions: ["desc1", "desc2", "desc3"],
        icons: ["icon1", "icon2", "icon3" ],
        type: 'checkbox',
    }
}
```

#### `uiSchema.options`
`uiSchema.options` specific to `hub-field-input-tile-select`:

| option | type | required | default | description | 
| ------ | ---- | -------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `type` | `"radio" | "checkbox"` | `false` | `radio` | dictates if the field should be rendered in radio or checkbox mode
| `layout` | `"vertical" | "horizontal"` | `false` | `vertical` | dictates if the tile group should be rendered horizontally or vertically

The `hub-multiselect` component renders an input for the user to type in new string value and chips for selected values.

The user can type in new value in the input box and press the `Enter` button to add the value. If the value is alread selected, the component does nothing.

The user can click on the `x` button of the chip for the existing value. It will remove the value from the selection.

If disabled, the component will disable the input and remove the close button from chips. This prevents the user from interacting with the component and making changes to the selected values.
